title: Plans and spending — try the built interface

steps.path: The proposed card in chat · before the spending rework
steps.headline: Open the old card and inspect its per-step budgets, ceiling and Approve control.
steps.changed: Before: each step has its own allowance; the proposal shows a ceiling and no spending gear.
steps.notice: This is the real earlier renderer at revision 3bb875300. Next shows the same conversation after the rework.
steps.risk: The workbench backend is simulated; neither revision runs specialists or charges anything.

steps.headline: Open the steps and the gear on the priced plan.
steps.changed: The card estimates a usual dollar range, rather than dividing an allowance among specialists.
steps.notice: The gear opens settings for this particular plan; Approve starts it without a limit unless you add one.
steps.risk: Simulated backend: clicking here spends nothing and does not run specialists.

steps.headline: Turn the spending limit on, enter a low amount, and change a step’s model.
steps.changed: A named popup holds one optional limit for the whole plan and individual step models.
steps.notice: Try $1 against the usual $0.40–$2 range; the low-limit warning appears. Turn the limit back off too.
steps.risk: These settings are simulated locally in this pane.

steps.headline: Look at the estimate when specialists use your ChatGPT plan.
steps.changed: The card uses an approximate amount of usage instead of claiming a dollar price.
steps.notice: The line says the usage is included in your ChatGPT plan.
steps.risk: This is a fixture, not a signed-in ChatGPT run.

steps.headline: Look at the estimate when specialists run on your computer.
steps.changed: Unpriced work shows an approximate usage amount, not an invented dollar figure.
steps.notice: The estimate says it runs on your computer.
steps.risk: No local model runs inside this review.

steps.headline: Expand the long plan and check the specialist assignments and gear.
steps.changed: A heavy plan uses the same settings and estimate treatment as a short plan.
steps.notice: Check the longest titles and expanded steps for overflow or missing controls.
steps.risk: This plan is illustrative, not a real audit.

steps.path: The running card in chat · before the spending rework
steps.headline: Inspect the old per-step limits and usage before the new running total.
steps.changed: Before: a specialist's budget was a separate allowance rather than one optional plan limit.
steps.notice: The next slide shows live spend beside Stop the plan in the same card.
steps.risk: The old renderer is interactive here, but the work is simulated.

steps.headline: See the live dollar total and the Stop the plan control.
steps.changed: The running card shows spend instead of per-step allowances; with no limit there is no ceiling.
steps.notice: Open the gear to see that you can set a whole-plan limit while work runs.
steps.risk: Spend in this pane is seeded, not a measured live charge.

steps.headline: Compare dollars spent with the whole-plan dollar limit.
steps.changed: The running row says how much was spent out of the chosen total.
steps.notice: Try the gear; a step that already started cannot change models, but an unstarted step can.
steps.risk: The workbench changes only its own simulated plan.

steps.headline: Check that an unpriced run reports usage instead of dollars.
steps.changed: The same running controls work when there is no published dollar rate.
steps.notice: Open settings to inspect the alternative limit unit.

steps.path: The paused card in chat · before the spending rework
steps.headline: Inspect the old Add budget action before trying the new Continue amount box.
steps.changed: Before: a paused specialist asked for more of its own allowance.
steps.notice: The next slide asks for a new total plan limit only when a whole-plan limit was reached.
steps.risk: These workbench controls do not start a real run.

steps.headline: Enter a new total limit in the Continue box and try the amount field.
steps.changed: At the limit the plan pauses once and offers Stop or Continue; Continue asks for a new total limit.
steps.notice: The Continue box is open. Enter a number above what was spent, then continue; completed specialists stay complete.
steps.risk: Resume is simulated; no specialist is launched here.

steps.path: The completed card and reply in chat
steps.headline: Read the completed plan alongside the assistant’s ordinary reply.
steps.changed: After the specialists finish, the assistant receives their final reports and answers in chat.
steps.notice: The answer is a normal assistant message, not another plan card.
steps.risk: The reply is scripted for review, not model-generated.

steps.path: The fourth step on the proposed card
steps.headline: Find the step that gathers reports from steps 1, 2 and 3.
steps.changed: One combining step can consume several earlier steps instead of seeing just one report.
steps.notice: Open the fourth step and check its incoming-source label.
steps.risk: This shows the card’s data shape; the backend is not run here.

steps.headline: Inspect a plan awaiting your decision after interruption.
steps.changed: Restarted plans wait for Continue instead of silently repeating work.
steps.notice: The card offers recovery actions; Stop is available when you do not want to proceed.
steps.risk: This pane starts in an interrupted fixture, not an actual restarted process.

steps.path: Settings → Assistant settings → Specialists · before the spending rework
steps.headline: Inspect the old automatic plan approval threshold, then compare it with the next slide.
steps.changed: Before: the automatic approval threshold was measured in tokens rather than dollars.
steps.notice: The earlier app's Specialists page opens here; the setting remains clickable.
steps.risk: Settings in this workbench pane are simulated and do not change your installed app.

steps.headline: Find the automatic plan-start row and try its threshold.
steps.changed: Automatic start depends on the estimated dollar amount; larger plans still ask first.
steps.notice: The Specialists page opens here; switch it on and enter a dollar amount. Unpriced plans still ask first.
steps.risk: The setting here is simulated and unpriced plans never auto-start.
